title: Building the WPA band from relief rolls
summary: He began playing trumpet to fill the unit, recruited men from relief and then had the cream of the crop.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: And you got the band together.
How many men were in the band?
Well, when I first started, in order to keep the -- have the unit to operate, I had to play trumpet for a while, until I could get enough trumpet players so I could stand up and direct.
And it started out with -- oh, I guess, piano, three or four -- four-string guitars --
Yeah, and a trombone, drums, one saxophone, and, you see, you didn't have too much to pick from because of the fact the people that you had to get, theywould have to be relief status.
Was there still a lot of paying jobs around then, for musicians?
No, this was during rough times. And what you had to do, you'd have to go out and recruit men, good men, and then get them on relief and then have them transferred
off of relief to the WPA.
Music project. That's the only way they'd have to show whether they are on relief. So after I found out what to do, then I had the cream of the crop. And I had a band. I picked some of the best men.
